title: Refugees get 10 days to contest status termination
description: A final work-permit rule takes effect, Texas investigates an ICE vehicle strike, and San Antonio challenges a proposed detention site.
body_md:
*A new USCIS rule cuts the response period in refugee-status termination proceedings from 30 days to 10, while leaving unclear how many people will ultimately face those proceedings.*

## Refugees get 10 days to contest termination of status

**USCIS has reduced the time refugees have to contest the proposed termination of their status from 30 days to 10.** The interim final rule takes effect Oct. 14 and is intended, the administration says, to address cases in which people were admitted despite being ineligible for refugee status. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/refugiados-eeuu-estatus-plazo-reduccion-trump-96817a38b6ab700beeab383ce2444a73)

The administration is reviewing cases involving refugees admitted during the Biden administration whose green-card applications remain pending. But the rule does not establish how many people will receive termination notices, and a shortened response period is not itself a termination of status or a removal order. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6146525-trump-administration-rule-refugees), [Newsday](https://newsday.com/news/nation/trump-refugees-immigration-deportation-i79289)

## Automatic work-permit extensions end as DHS separately proposes tougher repeat reviews

**A final DHS rule ending automatic work-permit extensions for many renewal applicants takes effect upon publication Oct. 14.** Workers covered by the change can face gaps in employment authorization if USCIS has not decided their renewal applications before their current permits expire. DHS says eliminating the extensions will allow more frequent vetting; the extensions had been intended to prevent processing delays from forcing people out of work. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/daily-labor-report/dhs-rule-nixes-automatic-extension-of-immigrant-work-permits)

Separately, DHS has proposed ending general deference to prior USCIS approvals in certain nonimmigrant worker-extension cases. That proposal is not final and does not change current policy yet. [Fragomen](https://news.google.?oc=5)

## Texas prosecutor says an ICE vehicle strike may have been intentional

**Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare says video collected by local investigators appears to show an ICE officer intentionally striking Miguel Parra Hernandez with a vehicle during an enforcement operation.** Teare said his office is investigating a possible aggravated-assault charge and accused federal authorities of failing to cooperate fully or preserve potential vehicle data. No charging decision or final adjudication has been made. [NBC News](https://nbcnews.com/news/us-news/texas-da-says-ice-intentionally-hit-immigrant-car-may-withheld-evidenc-rcna603243)

ICE disputes the prosecutor’s account, calling allegations that the officer acted intentionally false. The agency initially said Parra ran in front of the vehicle and was struck. DHS told NBC News that ICE officers wore body cameras and that the agency was reviewing video as part of an internal investigation. Parra suffered multiple fractures and remained in federal custody, according to the report.

## San Antonio sues to block a proposed ICE detention site

**San Antonio has filed a federal lawsuit seeking to halt conversion of an East Side warehouse into an immigration detention facility until DHS and ICE complete an environmental review.** The city says the agencies failed to comply with the National Environmental Policy Act and asks the court to stop development while the required assessment is conducted. The lawsuit does not challenge the federal government’s authority to enforce immigration law. [City of San Antonio](https://sa.gov/Directory/News-Releases/City-Files-Legal-Action-Regarding-Proposed-ICE-Detention-Facility)

The city also alleges violations of the Administrative Procedure Act and says federal officials have provided little information about the project’s environmental, infrastructure and community effects. Filing the lawsuit does not itself stop the project; the court has not ruled on the requested relief. [Texas Tribune](https://texastribune.org/2026/10/13/dhs-ice-warehouse-san-antonio-lawsuit-environmental-impact)

## Judge calls the federal voter-data effort an unlawful dragnet

**A federal judge has vacated a Justice Department policy that collected state voter records, shared data with immigration authorities and checked the records against federal citizenship information.** Judge Sparkle Sooknanan ruled in a challenge brought by Common Cause that the nationwide policy exceeded DOJ’s authority and violated the Privacy Act, among other findings. [Court opinion](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.291580/gov.uscourts.dcd.291580.51.0_1.pdf), [Arizona Mirror](https://azmirror.com/2026/10/13/repub/trumps-voter-data-collection-scheme-is-an-illegal-nationwide-dragnet-judge-rules)

The ruling addresses the challenged federal policy, not every dispute over voter rolls or states’ own use of citizenship-verification systems. A Justice Department spokesperson told Arizona Mirror that the department was reviewing the decision.

## Around the system

- **About 500 people were participating in a hunger strike at Georgia’s Folkston ICE Processing Center, according to family members and legal representatives.** Participants were protesting detention conditions and what they described as violations of asylum procedures; those claims remain allegations. [Georgia Public Broadcasting and The Current](https://gpb.org/news/2026/10/13/approximately-500-participate-in-hunger-strike-at-folkston-immigration-detention)

- **Civil-rights groups sued DHS over conditions at Camp East Montana, the detention site at Fort Bliss.** The complaint alleges physical abuse, sexual harassment, inadequate medical care, spoiled food and punitive isolation; the allegations have not been adjudicated. [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/US/aclu-sues-dhs-inhumane-conditions-nations-largest-immigration/story?id=133492027)

- **Costa Rican authorities are investigating reports that children ages 9 and 11 were held at the Dilley family detention facility in Texas.** Available records did not say whether a parent or guardian accompanied them, and their current circumstances were unclear. [The Tico Times](https://ticotimes.net/2026/10/13/ice-costa-rican-children-dilley-texas-detention), [Repretel](https://repretel.com/noticia/que-se-sabe-sobre-los-ninos-ticos-detenidos-por-el-ice-en-ee-uu)

- **ICE acknowledged immediately rearresting some people at Minnesota’s Whipple federal building after judges ordered their release.** MPR News reported that court records and statements by ICE officials indicate the practice extends beyond the three people interviewed. [MPR News](https://mprnews.org/story/2026/10/13/ice-admits-instant-rearrest-strategy)

- **Seven people released from immigration detention filed a proposed class action alleging that ICE failed to return money, phones, identity documents and other property.** The complaint seeks an order requiring the return of property and an end to the alleged practice; its claims have not been adjudicated. [ACLU of Illinois](https://aclu-il.org/press-releases/people-released-from-immigration-detention-sue-ice-for-refusing-to-return-their-property)

- **A local nonprofit counted 114 people detained during a weeklong federal operation across California’s San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara and Ventura counties.** The Department of Homeland Security did not respond to the outlet’s questions about the increased activity. [San Luis Obispo Tribune](https://sanluisobispo.com/news/local/article317562167.html)

- **A UCLA–UC Berkeley project found that nearly 15,000 people arrested in seven Southern California counties were deported between January 2025 and August 2026.** The analysis used immigration-enforcement records obtained from ICE. [Deportation Data Project](https://deportationdata.org/analysis/immigration-enforcement-in-los-angeles-second-trump-administration.html)

- **Lawyers say the man shot by ICE in New York remains in federal custody with a bullet lodged in his neck and needs specialist care.** DHS has defended the underlying operation, saying the officer fired after the vehicle moved toward agents. [El Diario NY](https://eldiariony.com/2026/10/13/inmigrante-baleado-por-ice-en-nueva-york-sigue-en-prision-con-un-proyectil-en-el-cuello-segun-abogados), [Documented](https://documentedny.com/2026/10/13/agente-ice-dispara-marble-hill)

- **ICE acknowledged bringing detainees to the parking lot of a Roxbury, New Jersey, warehouse for initial processing on two days in September.** The agency said they were not taken inside and that its Newark field office later ordered agents to stop bringing people to the site. [Gothamist](https://gothamist.com/news/ice-admits-to-using-roxbury-nj-warehouse-site-to-process-immigrants)

- **Immigration arrests linked to searches of Washington driver information increased at least fivefold since July, according to University of Washington researchers.** Their count rose from 64 verified cases over roughly a year to 354 as of Tuesday. [The Seattle Times](https://seattletimes.com/seattle-news/law-justice/immigration-arrests-linked-to-wa-driver-data-off-the-charts)

- **Records reviewed by Louisville Public Media show Indiana State Police helping enforce immigration rules against commercial truck drivers.** The reporting distinguishes state traffic stops and arrests from the later transfer of drivers into federal immigration custody. [Louisville Public Media](https://lpm.org/investigate/2026-10-13/indiana-state-police-help-drive-trumps-crackdown-on-immigrant-truckers-records-show)

- **The Hampden County sheriff’s office regularly sent jail-roster information to ICE for more than two years, according to records obtained by The Shoestring.** The office says it stopped the daily disclosures after Massachusetts’ PROTECT Act took effect but will continue its partnership with Homeland Security Investigations. [The Shoestring](https://theshoestring.org/2026/10/13/records-hampden-sheriffs-office-regularly-sent-jail-roster-to-ice)

- **The New York attorney general is reviewing whether North Tonawanda police improperly collaborated with Border Patrol in the detention of three roofers.** The police chief said any appearance of coordination was coincidental; advocates and the men’s lawyer contend that the encounter may have violated new state restrictions. [Investigative Post](https://investigativepost.org/2026/10/13/north-tonawanda-arrest-of-migrants-tests-new-law)

- **Petaluma unanimously adopted a resolution limiting municipal cooperation and resource sharing with federal immigration enforcement.** The policy restricts use of city property, access to nonpublic areas and voluntary data sharing. [KZST](https://kzst.com/2026/10/13/petaluma-city-council-passes-strict-limits-on-ice-cooperation)

- **Burien, Washington, unanimously approved a resolution strengthening local protections for immigrants.** It bars city cooperation with civil immigration enforcement without a judicial warrant, prohibits city contracts with ICE and restricts enforcement activity on city property. [KIRO 7](https://kiro7.com/news/local/burien-city-council-unanimously-approves-resolution-strengthening-immigrant-protections/YCLJWFHZ6BCWNMTE4H7FALNSHY/)

email.preview: A final work-permit rule takes effect, Texas investigates an ICE vehicle strike, and San Antonio sues over a proposed detention site.

upcoming.text: People who got a green card through marriage and hold it on a two-year conditional basis have to apply to make it permanent (Form I-751, Petition to Remove the Conditions on Residence). USCIS is seeking approval for a revised version of that form and is taking public comments until October 14, 2026.

DHS is raising two immigration enforcement fees created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (HR-1) to $5,300 each for fiscal year 2027. They apply to people arrested after being ordered deported at a hearing they missed (in absentia), and to people caught crossing between official ports of entry.

USCIS raises several fees: the first work permit for people with asylum, parole or TPS cases (Form I-765) goes from $560 to $570, and the TPS application — protection from deportation for people from countries in crisis (Form I-821) — from $510 to $520, among others. Anything postmarked on or after that date with the old fee is rejected.

upcoming.text: Employers who sponsor H-1B workers may face scrutiny of past filings: a September 18 executive order gives the Labor Department's Wage and Hour Division 30 days to start mining data from labor condition applications already filed — the wage and working-condition promises an employer makes before hiring an H-1B worker (LCA) — to decide whether to open investigations.

upcoming.text: Work permits (EADs) belonging to people from Ukraine and Sudan who have protection from deportation because their country is in crisis (TPS) are automatically extended only through October 19, 2026, while renewal applications are pending. Unless USCIS issues a further extension notice before then, employers will need to reverify those workers on Form I-9.

The immigration courts (EOIR) are updating the forms someone already in deportation proceedings files to ask a judge to let them stay and keep or get a green card (cancellation of removal) — Form EOIR-42A for current green card holders, Form EOIR-42B for everyone else. Comments are open until October 19, 2026.
